title: Quantum-vulnerable algorithm transition (NIST IR 8547, final)
$comment: An example policy, not advice. It applies the transition schedule of NIST IR 8547 (final, 27 October 2026) to the algorithms a CBOM discloses. Quantum-vulnerable signature and key-establishment algorithms are deprecated after 2030 and disallowed after 2035, at every approved security strength. The schedule is data in this file; the evaluation method is implemented by evaluate_policy.py. The judgement is computed at evaluation time and recorded in a result that points to the CBOM by digest, never stored in the CBOM. Check the schedule against the NIST publication before relying on it.

source.title: NIST IR 8547, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards

schedule.note: The final report deprecates quantum-vulnerable algorithms after 2030 at every approved strength; the 2024 draft deprecated only 112-bit strength.

changelog.summary: The classification moves to the shared set pkic.example.classification.algorithms 0.1, referred to by digest under classificationSource. The entries are unchanged, so every result is the same apart from the policy version and digest. Adds interpretation: mechanical, because the schedule is a set of dates and strengths taken from the source without judgement.

Adds the CycloneDX cryptography registry form of each name the examples now use (for example RSA-PKCS1-1.5-SHA-256 beside RS256, ECDHE-secp384r1 beside secp384r1), with the same classification. The earlier names are kept, so records that use them classify as before.
Follows the final NIST IR 8547 (27 October 2026): quantum-vulnerable algorithms at 128 bits and above are now deprecated after 2030, as at 112 bits.
